text: {"final": {"findings": [{"id": "R1", "statement": "registry/dedup.py already provides the duplicate detection the ticket needs: find_duplicates(households: list[Household]) -> list[list[str]] returns groups of 2+ ACTIVE household IDs that are the same family, each group sorted by ID. Same-family test is same_family(a, b): name_key(a.head.name) == name_key(b.head.name) and a.head.birth_year == b.head.birth_year.", "file": "registry/dedup.py"}, {"id": "R2", "statement": "name_key(name: str) -> tuple[str, ...] splits the name on whitespace and returns the Soundex code of each part; soundex(word) returns the American Soundex code (first letter + 3 digits, e.g. 'Robert' -> 'R163'). This is how 'Mohamed Ali' and 'Muhammad Ali' match.", "file": "registry/dedup.py"}, {"id": "R3", "statement": "core/ids.py provides is_valid_household_id(household_id: str) -> bool: True for IDs matching r\"HH-(\\d{4})(\\d)\" where the last digit equals household_check_digit(base). household_check_digit(base: str) -> int | None computes a mod-11 check digit with weights (5, 4, 3, 2) and returns None when the result would be 10 (such bases are never issued).", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R4", "statement": "registry/register.py provides set_status(household_id: str, status: str, *, merged_into: str | None = None) -> Household. It validates status is one of ('active', 'inactive', 'merged'), sets h.status and h.merged_into on the matching record, saves the whole list, and returns the Household; raises KeyError if the ID is not found. This marks a duplicate as merged without deleting it.", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "load_households(*, active_only: bool = False) -> list[Household] reads data/registry.json (key 'households', via store.read_json(REGISTRY) with REGISTRY = 'registry.json') and returns all records, or only those with status == 'active' when active_only=True. save_households(households: list[Household]) rewrites the file using h.to_dict().", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R6", "statement": "Household fields: id, region, site, phone, members (members[0] is the head, with .name and .birth_year property), registered (ISO date), status ('active' | 'inactive' | 'merged', default 'active'), sms_ok, shelter_damaged, income_lost, disability, merged_into (str | None). Household.from_dict(d) / to_dict() convert to/from the JSON dict form.", "file": "core/models.py"}, {"id": "R7", "statement": "Downstream consumers already filter on status == 'active' (load_households(active_only=True)), so marking duplicates as 'merged' stops double rations without deleting records: distribution/planner.py:32 iterates load_households(active_only=True), and tests/test_registry.py:32 asserts a merged ID is absent from load_households(active_only=True).", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R8", "statement": "Script conventions: ops scripts live in scripts/ and must add the repo root to sys.path (sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))) before importing project modules; scripts that change data/registry.json must say so in their docstring (scripts/stock_report.py is the read-only example, run as 'python scripts/stock_report.py' from the Lifeline root).", "file": "scripts/stock_report.py"}, {"id": "R9", "statement": "next_household_id(households: list[Household] | None = None) -> str exists if a kept record ever needs a new ID: it takes max(int(h.id[3:7])) + 1 (default 999) and skips bases where household_check_digit returns None, returning make_household_id(number).", "file": "registry/register.py"}]}}
